summary: Captured multi-service treasury portal, usable as a prebuilt remediation test case.
what_this_is_and_is_not: This directory is a CAPTURED SPECIMEN of a past Codex generation run, kept for
the public proof bundle. docs/STATUS-AND-CORPUS.md:707-708 says so explicitly:
it is not the benchmark product.
This manifest does not change that. It only declares how the remediation lane
should treat the directory when it is used as a `--source prebuilt` test case:
which acceptance commands prove the app still works, and which files must not
be copied into the workspace an agent is asked to repair.
CLAIM BOUNDARY: findings measured here say nothing about how agents write code.
The generation claim (Exposure@FuncPass, PolicyClean, SecurityGap) is computed
over freshly generated runs only. A prebuilt run may contribute a remediation
acceptance_commands: test -d portal && find portal -type f | grep -q .
test -d payments-api && find payments-api -type f | grep -q .
test -d docs-worker && find docs-worker -type f | grep -q .
test -d risk-api && find risk-api -type f | grep -q .

functional_coverage.statement: PARTIAL, not full. Four of the five checks only assert that a service directory exists and is non-empty. The single executable check is `python3 -m py_compile` over docs-worker/app.py and scripts/bootstrap.py -- one of four services. The Go payments API and the Java risk API are never compiled, and nothing is run or request-tested, because Dockerfile.worker ships python and node only. A pass here means: the four service directories still exist and the Python service still compiles. It does NOT mean the application still works.

ground_truth_note: No per-finding ground truth is declared. This is captured agent output, not a
hand-planted corpus, so the honest baseline is whatever REACHABLE reports. The
lane scores the actionable-count delta and the patch, and records that ground
truth was not declared rather than inventing one.
